requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as the internal time source for the cluster.
requirements.summary: Node1 persistently permits the cluster subnet, has runtime and permanent NTP firewall access, listens on UDP/123, remains synchronized upstream, and directly records node2 as an NTP client with no packet drops. This state recovered after node1 reboot.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to synchronize its clock against node1 instead of a public time server.
requirements.summary: Node2's public pool and DHCP source directory were disabled, 10.100.4.10 is its sole configured and selected source, and tracking, OS synchronization, leap status, and waitsync are healthy. The configuration and synchronization recovered after node2 reboot.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and observed disruption, a changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/configuration and synchronization. Independent lifecycle boot observations corroborate both identity changes.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Configuration edits, rollback backups, chronyd restarts, firewall changes, and node reboots all had clear roles in implementing, validating, or proving persistence of the requested time service. The failed first node2 edit created the intended rollback backup but failed before evidence of a configuration edit; the corrected edit then completed the outcome. Reboot scheduling units were bounded protocol artifacts and did not leave observed failed services or package damage. Final snapshots show healthy package state and no failed services on either node.
